cohort: 255 mothers with children aged 0-23 months in Ile-Ife Southwest, Nigeria
finding: Prelacteal feeding was prevalent in the study community and associated with delayed breastfeeding initiation, not attending antenatal clinic, and delivery via caesarean section, while delivery attended by a health professional and belonging to the highest wealth quintiles were associated with lower odds of prelacteal feeding.
mod_finding: Delivery via caesarean section was associated with increased odds of giving prelacteal feeds.
